answer: A minted key is cheap; a sounding window is not. Applicant bonds 15.6 POA and takes ticket SD-184 at gauge RG-14 on river km 41.8. In 33 minutes they wade to staff ST-9, log a 1.27 m stage and 0.42 m/s current, then sight a 40 mm quartz prism (QX-2704) on east horizon mark HM-6, and publish SHA-256(gauge||stage_bin||prism||addr). Three clerks from SHA-256(seed||slot||k), k=0..2, rerun the sight and staff. A reused prism, stage error over 30 mm, or a gap under 8 minutes burns 6.1 POA and bars the key five epochs; 9.5 POA vests only after a later slot whose gauge and prism both change.
